claims.text: The Cu matrix has a native surface oxide layer.
A compositionally graded interlayer transitioning from Cu to the target HEA will improve HEA-to-Cu adhesion.
Improved HEA-to-Cu adhesion produced by the graded interlayer will enhance the composite's wear resistance.
Cr is a Cu-compatible interlayer element that can tailor interfacial bonding and mitigate thermal-expansion mismatch.
The graded interlayer bridges chemical and thermal-property differences between Cu and the HEA.
The transitional bonding zone ensures continuous and stable interfacial bonding.
Gradually varying composition from Cu to the HEA reduces abrupt changes in thermal-expansion coefficient and chemical reactivity.
The graded composition improves mechanical interlocking and chemical bonding at the Cu–HEA interface.
The graded interlayer reduces interfacial stress concentrations.
A graded-interlayer specimen will have significantly greater adhesion than an HEA coating deposited directly on Cu.
A graded-interlayer specimen will have greater wear resistance under operational stress than an HEA coating deposited directly on Cu.
Direct deposition of an HEA coating on Cu is expected to produce poor adhesion and possible delamination because of thermal-expansion and surface-chemistry mismatches.
Interlayer thickness, composition gradient, deposition technique, and operating temperature can limit the effectiveness of the graded-interlayer strategy.
Interlayer reactions may adversely affect coating performance.
Post-deposition annealing and interfacial optimization have been shown to improve HEA-coating adhesion.
